title: Multi-Level Marketing
overview: This five-day course examines multi-level marketing (MLM) as a relationship-based direct selling model, focusing on ethical customer acquisition, product-led sales, distributor development, team leadership, and sustainable business practices. Participants explore how compensation structures, recruitment, retention, and sales activities interact; distinguish legitimate product-based direct selling from unlawful pyramid schemes; and apply practical tools for compliant communication, customer protection, financial planning, and performance management. The program emphasizes realistic earnings representations, transparent selling, and long-term customer value.
audience: Direct selling professionals and independent distributors seeking structured commercial skills.
Sales team leaders, field supervisors, and network development managers.
Business development, channel sales, and distribution professionals.
Entrepreneurs evaluating or managing a product-based direct selling model.
Sales trainers, compliance coordinators, and customer experience personnel supporting distributor networks.
methodology: Facilitated discussions, direct-selling case studies, compensation-plan interpretation exercises, customer discovery and sales role-plays, ethical recruitment simulations, team coaching practice, performance dashboard workshops, and a final business action-plan presentation. Scenarios emphasize consumer protection and realistic commercial outcomes.
competencies: Understanding MLM structures, direct selling economics, and distributor responsibilities.
Ethical prospecting, consultative selling, customer service, and relationship development.
Clear product communication and compliant earnings and opportunity disclosures.
Distributor onboarding, training, coaching, engagement, and retention.
Sales planning, activity management, unit economics, and performance analysis.
Risk recognition, consumer protection, and sustainable network leadership.
objectives: Explain the mechanics, strengths, and limitations of product-based multi-level marketing.
Distinguish retail customer demand from recruitment-driven activity and recognize pyramid-scheme warning signs.
Evaluate compensation plans, expenses, margins, and realistic earning scenarios.
Conduct ethical prospecting, discovery, demonstrations, and follow-up.
Communicate product claims and income opportunities accurately without pressure or exaggeration.
Design effective distributor onboarding, training, and coaching processes.
Track customer retention, retail sales, conversion, and distributor productivity.
Develop a compliant, measurable business and team development plan.
